'''Ingo Potrykus''' (born 5 December 1933) is a German biologist who is Professor Emeritus of Plant Sciences at the Institute of Plant Sciences of the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]] (ETH), Zurich from which he retired in 1999. His [[research]] group applied gene technology to contribute to food security in developing countries. Together with [[Peter Beyer (professor)|Peter Beyer]], he is one of the co-inventors of [[golden rice]]. In 2014 he was chairman of the Golden Rice Humanitarian Board.<ref name="rice">(2014) [http://www.goldenrice.org Golden Rice Project, Golden Rice Humanitarian Board] Official web page of the Golden Rice Project, Retrieved 2 March 2014</ref>

==Education and career==
Potrykus studied [[biology]] at the [[University of Cologne]] and earned his [[doctorate]] at the [[Max-Planck Institute]] for Plant Breeding Research, Cologne, Germany. After several years at the Institute of Plant Physiology, [[University of Hohenheim]], he became research group leader at the Max-Planck Institute for Plant Genetics. Ladenburg, Germany.<ref name = CV>[http://fbae.org/2009/FBAE/website/governing-body_ingo.html Prof. Ingo Potrykus, CV] FBAE, Retrieved 2 March 2014</ref> In 1976 he transferred to [[Basel]], Switzerland to establish the area of plant [[genetic engineering]] at the [[Friedrich Miescher Institute]].<ref name="rice" /> In 1986 he became professor of plant sciences at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, concentrating on the [[Biotechnology]] of Plants.<ref name = Handbook>Newton, David "DNA Technology: A Reference Handbook" 12 November 2009, Pages 161 - 162, ABC-CLIO  publishers, {{ISBN|978-1598843286}}</ref> He retired from this institute in 1999 at the age of 65.<ref name = Time>Nash, Madeleine J. (31 July 200) [http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,997586,00.html This Rice Could Save a Million Kids a Year] Time Magazine, Retrieved 2 march 2014</ref>

==Research==

Motivated by the upcoming food crisis problem of [[malnutrition]] in [[developing countries]] and the potential of [[gene]] technology to contribute to food security, Potrykus and his research group dedicated their work to genetic engineering projects aimed at improving yield stability and food quality of crops such as [[rice]], [[wheat]], [[millet]], [[sorghum]], and [[cassava]].<ref>Weasel, Lisa H. 2009. "Food Fray" Amacom Publishing, {{ISBN|978-0814401644}}</ref> The most significant development so far has been the creation of golden rice, a new rice variety providing [[vitamin A]]. This strain of rice is widely seen as the model example of how to sustainably reduce malnutrition in developing countries. Potrykus began thinking about using genetic engineering to improve the nutritional qualities of rice in the late 1980s. He knew that of some 3 billion people who depend on rice as their staple crop, around 10% risk some level of vitamin A deficiency. This problem interested Potrykus for numerous reasons, including the scientific challenge of transferring not just a single gene, but a group of genes that represented a key part of a biochemical pathway. In 1993, with funding from the [[Rockefeller Foundation]], Potrykus teamed up with [[Peter Beyer (professor)|Peter Beyer]] and they launched what would become a seven-year, $2.6 million project to develop Golden Rice.<ref>Robinson, Simon [http://content.time.com/time/world/article/0,8599,2047898,00.html Grains of Hope] Time Magazine, 31 July 2000. Web</ref>

Since his retirement in 1999, Ingo Potrykus - as president of the International Humanitarian Golden Rice Board - has devoted his energy to guiding Golden Rice towards [[subsistence]] farmers across the many hurdles of a GMO-crop. To this end he has been established collaboration with 14 rice institutions in [[India]], [[China]], [[Vietnam]], [[Bangladesh]], [[Indonesia]], and [[Philippines]].  In 2013 Potrykus met the Pope who offered his personal blessing to Golden Rice although the Pope was concerned that genetic modification benefited big business rather than the poor.<ref>Spady, Tyrone (January/February 2014) [http://newsletter.aspb.org/2014/janfeb14.pdf Pope Blesses Golden Rice] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140412061655/http://newsletter.aspb.org/2014/janfeb14.pdf |date=2014-04-12 }} ASBP News, Volume 41, Number 1, Page 11, Retrieved 2 March 2014</ref>

==Personal life==
Potrykus has been married since 1960 to Inge Heilingbrunner.<ref name = Vatican>(2008) [https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_academies/acdscien/sito%20fino%202011/2008/potrykus2008.pdf Ingo Potrykus] Vatican Yearbook 2008, Pontifical Academy of Sciences, Retrieved 2 march 2014</ref>  He has three children and eight grandchildren.<ref name = rice/>
